name: The gradual training (anupubbasikkhā) of the Sāmaññaphala and related suttas

stages.name: tathāgatuppāda, dhammassavana
stages.gloss: a Tathāgata arises; hearing the Dhamma
stages.description: A Tathāgata arises and teaches; a householder hears the Dhamma and gains faith.

stages.name: pabbajjā
stages.description: Seeing the household life as crowded, he goes forth into homelessness.

stages.name: sīla
stages.description: Restraint by the Pātimokkha and the short, middle and long sections on virtue; blameless happiness.

stages.name: indriyasaṃvara
stages.description: Not grasping at signs and features of sense objects.

stages.name: satisampajañña
stages.description: Full awareness in all activities.

stages.name: santuṭṭhi
stages.description: Content with robes and alms, like a bird with its wings.

stages.name: nīvaraṇappahāna
stages.description: In a secluded place, mindfulness established, he cleanses the mind of the five hindrances; gladness and joy arise.

stages.name: cattāri jhānāni
stages.description: The four absorptions with their similes of bodily pervasion.

stages.name: ñāṇadassana
stages.description: Directing the concentrated mind to see the body as material and consciousness as bound up with it.

stages.name: abhiññā
stages.gloss: mind-made body and the direct knowledges
stages.description: Mind-made body, psychic powers, divine ear, knowledge of others' minds, recollection of past lives, divine eye.

stages.name: āsavakkhayañāṇa
stages.gloss: knowledge of the destruction of the effluents
stages.description: Knowing the four truths and the effluents as they are; liberation and the knowledge 'birth is ended'.

summary: The step-by-step path from hearing the Dhamma to the destruction of the effluents, given in DN 2 and repeated with variations in DN 1–13, MN 27, MN 38, MN 39, MN 51, MN 107 and MN 125.
notes: Band B4 for the direct knowledges is an interpretation: the texts present them as attainments of the concentrated mind before the final knowledge, not as insight.

name: The proximate causes of liberation (Upanisa Sutta, SN 12.23)

stages.name: dukkha
stages.description: Suffering, the last link of the worldly series, is the proximate cause of faith.

stages.name: saddhā
stages.description: Faith, the proximate cause of gladness.

stages.name: pāmojja
stages.description: Gladness (in AN 11.1 arising from the non-remorse of virtue).

stages.name: pīti
stages.description: Rapture born of gladness.

stages.name: passaddhi
stages.description: Tranquillity of body and mind.

stages.name: sukha
stages.description: Happiness, the proximate cause of concentration.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Concentration.

stages.name: yathābhūtañāṇadassana
stages.gloss: knowledge and vision of things as they are
stages.description: Seeing things as they really are.

stages.name: nibbidā
stages.description: Disenchantment.

stages.name: virāga
stages.description: Dispassion.

stages.name: vimutti
stages.description: Liberation.

stages.name: khayeñāṇa
stages.description: Knowledge of the destruction of the effluents.

summary: The 'supporting conditions' that lead from suffering through faith and concentration to the knowledge of destruction; a parallel sequence from wholesome virtue (AN 11.1–2).
notes: 'Transcendental dependent origination' is a modern name for this sequence; the text's own word is upanisā.

name: The sixteen steps of mindfulness of breathing (MN 118)

stages.name: step 1
stages.description: Tetrad 1 (body): knowing long breaths; see prc:anapanasati-step-01.

stages.name: step 2
stages.description: Tetrad 1 (body): knowing short breaths; see prc:anapanasati-step-02.

stages.name: step 3
stages.description: Tetrad 1 (body): experiencing the whole body; see prc:anapanasati-step-03.

stages.name: step 4
stages.description: Tetrad 1 (body): calming the bodily formation; see prc:anapanasati-step-04.

stages.name: step 5
stages.description: Tetrad 2 (feelings): experiencing rapture; see prc:anapanasati-step-05.

stages.name: step 6
stages.description: Tetrad 2 (feelings): experiencing bliss; see prc:anapanasati-step-06.

stages.name: step 7
stages.description: Tetrad 2 (feelings): experiencing the mental formation; see prc:anapanasati-step-07.

stages.name: step 8
stages.description: Tetrad 2 (feelings): calming the mental formation; see prc:anapanasati-step-08.

stages.name: step 9
stages.description: Tetrad 3 (mind): experiencing the mind; see prc:anapanasati-step-09.

stages.name: step 10
stages.description: Tetrad 3 (mind): gladdening the mind; see prc:anapanasati-step-10.

stages.name: step 11
stages.description: Tetrad 3 (mind): concentrating the mind; see prc:anapanasati-step-11.

stages.name: step 12
stages.description: Tetrad 3 (mind): liberating the mind; see prc:anapanasati-step-12.

stages.name: step 13
stages.description: Tetrad 4 (dhammas): contemplating impermanence; see prc:anapanasati-step-13.

stages.name: step 14
stages.description: Tetrad 4 (dhammas): contemplating fading away; see prc:anapanasati-step-14.

stages.name: step 15
stages.description: Tetrad 4 (dhammas): contemplating cessation; see prc:anapanasati-step-15.

stages.name: step 16
stages.description: Tetrad 4 (dhammas): contemplating relinquishment; see prc:anapanasati-step-16.

summary: Four tetrads of breathing that fulfil the four establishments of mindfulness, the seven factors of awakening and true knowledge and liberation (MN 118; SN 54).
notes: Bands are an interpretation: the text itself does not map the steps onto stages; the fourth tetrad is contemplation leading to relinquishment.
